source.title: An assessment of data-centric methods for label noise identification in remote sensing data sets
source.authors: Felix Kröber; G. Hoxha; R. Roscher

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the full paper; no relevant sections appear cut off or garbled.
record.tranche_reason: Tests the effect of controlled label corruption on classification performance using a different setup from the random-label fitting claim. It reports test accuracy after training on noisy data, but does not report training error on the corrupted data.
record.gate_note: The study injects 10–70% structured or uniform noise into training labels and reports test performance. It does not report training error, convergence time, shuffled or noise inputs, regularization ablations, or learning dynamics. Cited statements about networks memorizing noisy labels are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: Section 4.2 directly tests V4's test-performance component in a new remote-sensing setting: clean-test accuracy decreases continuously as training-label corruption increases. Training-set fitting is untested, so these results bear on only part of V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that label noise harms generalization and data-centric filtering generally improves accuracy through 50% noise. They emphasize that noise identification, noise-level estimation, and downstream accuracy are only partially linked, and method choice depends on conditions and objectives.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains ResNet-18 models on remote-sensing data with injected label noise and evaluates data-centric filtering; it does not use the original random-label intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by data set, noise type, noise level, and filtering method.

fits_no_version.finding: TopoFilter, AuM, and confident learning detect and remove corrupted labels and generally improve clean-test accuracy through 50% corruption; benefits vary and can reverse at 70%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data-centric filtering can improve remote-sensing classification under label noise, with effectiveness depending on noise structure, corruption level, data set, and filtering method.

record.peer_reviewed: ISPRS Annals of the Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing and Spatial Information Sciences
record.problems: The paper reports test accuracy but not training error on the corrupted data, so it cannot establish whether the networks fit noisy labels. EuroSAT uses a subsampled 2.7K-image data set; experiments use three seeds per configuration. Results are primarily presented in figures, with selected aggregate changes stated in text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows qualify: the reported outcomes do not measure training-set fitting or another behavior named by the claim versions. Figure 5 and Sections 4.2–4.3 report test accuracy and filtering effects, but not training error on noisy labels.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, zero or near-zero training error, and chance test performance under unchanged training settings.
Relative time to fit true versus random labels and convergence rates across corruption levels.
Training-set fitting with shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect fitting of corrupted training sets, memorization of noise alongside remaining signal, and degradation through complete corruption to chance performance. Tested corruption levels are 10%, 30%, 50%, and 70%.
Effects of adding or removing weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Temporal ordering of learning real patterns and memorizing noise; no corresponding learning trajectories are reported.

missing.what: Extract unfiltered clean-test accuracy across corruption levels as evidence for V4's degradation component. The record explicitly excluded these results, but absence of training-error measurements does not exclude their bearing on the test-performance component.
missing.locator: Section 4.2 and Figure 5, plain baselines; Section 3.1 for training conditions.

record.verdict_notes: No existing rows require correction. The record's blanket exclusion of test-accuracy findings is too restrictive for V4. Filtering metrics and improvements do not establish random-label memorization, and descriptions of memorization or margin dynamics in the introduction and methods are not new empirical tests of V1 or V6.

versions.untested_parts: Whether standard networks fit completely random labels to zero or near-zero training error, and the corresponding test error.
Training time relative to true labels and convergence as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.
The study tests some corruption levels and reports test accuracy trends, but does not report whether the models fit the noisy training sets perfectly; it tests up to 70%, not all labels corrupted.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation affect fitting random labels, or whether removing them affects generalization on true labels.
Whether models learn real patterns before memorizing noisy or random labels over training.

relationships.condition: Unfiltered ResNet-18 training on UCMerced and subsampled EuroSAT, with uniform or asymmetric label corruption from 10% to 70%; test-performance component only.
relationships.reason: Based on Section 4.2 and Figure 5, with no extracted row ids: accuracy decreases continuously with increasing corruption across both data sets and all noise types. Reported accuracy gaps from clean-label training grow from 1.4–5.5 percentage points at 10% noise to 45.7–69.9 points at 70%.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy declined continuously across both datasets and all noise types, with gaps from clean-label training growing from 1.4–5.5 percentage points at 10% noise to 45.7–69.9 points at 70%.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
